Subject: Request: SIG/CAIQ VM evidence and SLA clarifications

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this — Fortiva is collecting SIG/CAIQ artifacts ahead of our audit. We need a compact vulnerability management evidence packet and a short attestation describing your scan cadence and remediation SLAs. Specifically:
- Latest authenticated scan index or sample export (csv)
- Confirmation of scheduled scan cadence (internal codebase, container images, infra)
- CVE remediation SLAs by severity and exception process
- A short playbook snippet describing hotfix steps (how you push fixes, canary rollout, verification)

Target: please send the packet and the attestation by EOD Nov 12 if possible. If anything needs to escalate to your security or compliance teams, loop them in.

Appreciate it — Sam Taylor
Compliance Manager, Fortiva Financial

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, compliance@fortiva.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: VM evidence packet and hotfix/playbook excerpt (internal + delivery)

Hi all — attaching the requested artifacts and a short summary below. Attachments: vm-scan-index-20261101.csv, cve-commitment-brief.pdf, hotfix-playbook.md (stubs).

Summary (high level):
- Scan cadence:
  * Authenticated full-scan (agents + container image verification): weekly on Wednesdays (internal code + infra).
  * Lightweight unauthenticated discovery scans: daily (quick surface-level checks for high-risk indicators).
  * Third-party dependency SBOM-based scanning: monthly, with exception window for urgent supply-chain CVEs.
  * Continuous host/agent telemetry for runtime detections (alerts forwarded to triage team).

- Triage & remediation SLA (default):
  * Critical (RCE/privilege escalation with exploitability): initial triage within 4 hours; mitigation or rollback plan within 48 hours. Mitigation may be WAF rule, emergency config change, or hotfix deploy.
  * High (critical business impact, patch available): triage within 24 hours; patch roll or mitigated workaround within 7 calendar days.
  * Medium: triage within 72 hours; remediation or scheduled backlog fix within 30 calendar days.
  * Low: scheduled during normal sprint planning, tracked in backlog.

- Exception process:
  * If remediation cannot meet SLA due to dependency constraints, engineering files an exception ticket (Jira SUP-XXXX) and escalates to Security + Product. For exceptions >14 days, CISO review required.

- Hotfix/playbook excerpt (process highlights):
  1) Create emergency branch and build container image with patch.
  2) Automated CI build -> image signed -> push to private registry.
  3) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 1 hour with health checks and expanded logs.
  4) If canary passes, progressive rollout in 25% increments with 15-minute verification windows and automated rollback on health degradation.
  5) Post-deploy verification: integration smoke tests + vulnerability rescan of canary group.

- Evidence links: sample scan index attached (vm-scan-index-20261101.csv). SOC2 evidence bucket also contains prior attestations: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-evidence

Notes: the attachments contain timestamps and sample CVE IDs and remediation traces. We can produce a signed attestation PDF on letterhead — Laura, can you prepare the attestation and sign-off?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Director, Security Operations | Redwood Inference
From: sam.taylor@fortiva.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VM evidence packet and hotfix/playbook excerpt (internal + delivery)

Kim/Team — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple quick clarifying questions before we close the SIG artifact:
1) For 'mitigation' within 48 hours on Critical: does that include backporting to older container tags (we have a few long-lived images)?
2) During the canary windows, do you run vulnerability rescan + functional smoke in an automated pipeline or are parts manual?
3) Fortiva will need the signed attestation to be uploaded to our DocuSign/secure portal — can you confirm who will own the signed PDF?

If you can answer those three items in a short note and attach the signed attestation, we'll be able to close the SIG/CAIQ question set.

Best,
Sam Taylor
Compliance Manager, Fortiva Financial
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: sam.taylor@fortiva.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VM evidence packet and hotfix/playbook excerpt (internal + delivery)

Hi Sam — quick answers below and attaching the signed attestation PDF to this thread (signed_attestation-fortiva-20261114.pdf).

1) Backports: yes — emergency backports to long-lived tags are part of our Critical response options when upstream patching is not feasible. We rebuild and sign the backported image, push to the private registry, and follow the same canary/rollout verification. We include CVE tracking for both mainline and backported tags in the remediation artifact.

2) Canary verification: the pipeline runs automated vulnerability rescan (container CVE quick-scan) and functional smoke tests during the canary window. Security telemetry and health checks are automated; engineering-runbook steps for manual verification are included if automated checks flag anomalies.

3) Signed attestation: Laura Bennett (Compliance) will own uploading the signed PDF to your DocuSign/secure portal. We will also add the signed PDF to the SOC2 evidence folder (link below) and provide HubSpot ticket reference: HubSpot-CR-48219.

Attached: signed_attestation-fortiva-20261114.pdf (stub)

If you need a separate letter on company letterhead with an exec signature, we can request C-level sign-off — let us know.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance | Redwood Inference
